example: There were 400 people at the meeting and they all, to a man, voted for the motion.
400人參加了會議，他們全都為這項動議投了贊成票。
That job would suit you to a tee.
那份工作完全適合你。
To some degree I think that's right, but there are other factors which affect the situation.
從某種程度上來講我認為那是對的，但是影響這種局面的還有其他因素。

NONE: C2 said when you feel that someone has made a bad situation worse by doing something else to upset you
雪上加霜；往傷口上撒鹽

example: They told me I was too old for the job, and then to add insult to injury, they refused to pay my expenses!
他們說我太老了，做不了這個工作。更讓人受不了的是，他們還拒絕支付我的費用！

NONE: › in one direction and then in the opposite direction, a number of times

example: She was gazing out the window, rocking rhythmically to and fro.
她注視著窗外，身體有節奏地來回搖晃著。

NONE: › worth taking seriously because of being powerful, important, or good
須重視的；須認真處理的

example: Are unions still a force to be reckoned with?
工會勢力依然需要受重視嗎？
Her new novel marks her as a writer to be reckoned with.
她的新小說讓她成為一個受重視的作者。
This is not his best book, to be sure, but it is still worth reading.
這本不是他寫得最好的書，這一點是肯定的，但還是值得一讀。

NONE: › used to mean that it is easy to understand what you could have done to prevent something bad from happening after it has happened
事後聰明很容易；放馬後炮很容易

example: In retrospect, we should have insisted on checking his calculations, but it's easy to be wise after the event.
回想起來，我們本該堅持檢查他的計算結果，不過事後聰明倒是容易。

NONE: B1 at the start of a process, event, or situation
B2 used to give the first important reason for something

example: There were six of us to begin with, then two people left.
原先，我們有6個人，後來走了兩個。
The hotel was awful! To begin with, our room was far too small.
這間飯店太差了！首先是我們的房間太小。
He's kind, handsome, and wealthy to boot.
他善良、英俊，還很富有。

NONE: C1 used when you mention something in addition to all the other (bad) things that have happened

example: It's been a terrible week and now, to cap it all, I've got a cold.
這一週真是糟透了，更倒楣的是，我現在又得了感冒。

NONE: › something you say before using an expression that has been very popular or used too much
套用一句流行的話；常言道；俗話說

example: I was, to coin a phrase, gobsmacked!
套用一句老話，我簡直目瞪口呆！

NONE: › used to say that something is the worst thing to happen in a series of unpleasant events

example: I had lost my ticket, was soaked to the skin, and, to crown it all, discovered that my purse had been stolen.
我把票弄丟了，又被淋得渾身濕透，最糟糕的是，我發現我的錢包被偷了。

NONE: B2 up to the present time

example: This novel is his best work to date.
這部小說是他迄今為止最好的作品。

NONE: › excellent or to be strongly wished for

example: She has a figure to die for.
她的身材特別棒。
That chocolate cake is to die for.
那個巧克力蛋糕非常誘人。
They sell beautiful shoes and to-die-for handbags.
他們售賣漂亮的鞋子和極美的手袋。
See also
to die for

NONE: › something that you say that means that it is natural for people to make mistakes and it is important to forgive people when they do
人皆犯錯（寬恕是德）；凡人多舛誤（唯神能見宥）； 人非聖賢，孰能無過
› an expression that means that you should praise someone who deserves it, although you might dislike some things about them

example: I don't especially like the woman but, credit where credit's due, she's very efficient.
我不是特別喜歡那個女人，不過，該說好的就說好，她辦事效率很高。

NONE: › to have achieved success and become famous

example: He felt he had truly arrived when he got his first part in a Broadway play.
他第一次在百老匯劇目中演出角色時，覺得自己真的成功了。

NONE: › If you wish or hope to hell that something is true or that it will happen, you are saying how strongly you want it to be true or to happen.

example: I hope to hell she hasn't missed that plane.
我非常希望她沒錯過那班飛機。

NONE: › mainly US informal also US the hell with sb/sth used to say that you do not care about someone or something
讓…見鬼去吧（表示不在意某人或某事）

example: I was ready to say the hell with it and leave.
我那時候已經想好要走了，讓它見鬼去吧。

NONE: › used when giving your opinion about the appearance of something or someone

example: You see, to my eye, she looks better without make-up.
哎，我反而覺得她不化妝更好看。
The room has pink walls and a green carpet, which to my mind looks all wrong.
牆壁刷成了粉紅色，鋪了一塊綠色的地毯，我覺得這根本不相配。

NONE: › used for saying that something is much more extreme than your words suggest
保守地說；說得好聽（或委婉）一點

example: It has been a remarkable day, to put it mildly.
說得委婉一點，這是不尋常的一天。

NONE: C2 and in addition there is
更不用說；而且還； 遑論

example: It would be an enormous amount of work, to say nothing of the cost.
工作量會很大，遑論費用了。

NONE: C1 used to show that what you are describing is in fact much more serious or important than you have suggested

example: It's going to be awkward, to say the least.
至少會很棘手。

NONE: C2 If you say something unpleasant to someone's face, you say it to them directly, when you are together.

example: If you've got something to say, say it to my face.
你要是有甚麼要說的，就當著我的面說。
To my way of thinking, the plan should never have been approved.
照我的想法，這個計劃根本不該批准的。

NONE: › UK having lost or spent a particular amount of money as a result of something

example: He ended the day £50 to the bad.
他那天虧了50英鎊。

NONE: › from what my memory tells me

example: To the best of my recollection I have never seen her before.
如果我沒記錯的話，我以前從來沒有見過她。

NONE: › all the way through, or very badly

example: I was frozen/chilled to the bone after waiting so long for the bus.
等公車等得太久了，我感到寒氣刺骨。

NONE: 徹頭徹尾的，完完全全的，完全的

example: He's a Conservative to the core.
他是個徹頭徹尾的保守分子。
I was shocked to the core.
我嚇壞了。
She died ten years ago to the day.
她正好在十年前的今天去世。

NONE: › used in expressions to mean completely full

example: By the time the fourth course was served, I was stuffed to the gills.
第四道菜上來的時候，我都已經飽極了。
The restaurant was packed to the gills.
這家飯店已經滿座。

NONE: 大多數人有利的，有益於多數人的，普遍有好處的

example: Greater international stability can surely only be to the good.
國際局勢更加穩定當然只會使世人獲益。

NONE: › If something is filled to the gunwales, it is extremely full.

example: A crowd of 50,000 packed the stadium almost to the gunwales.
五萬名觀眾將體育場擠得水泄不通。
Both sides have declared themselves ready to fight to the last man.
雙方都聲稱要戰鬥到底，直到最後一個人。

NONE: › until something is complete or has been achieved
› until the end of someone's life

example: I think my position is right, and I'll defend it to the last.
我認為自己的立場沒有錯，我會堅持到底。
She was a true patriot to the last.
她自始至終都是一位真正的愛國者。

NONE: › If you obey instructions or rules to the letter, you do exactly what you have been told to do, giving great attention to every detail.
一絲不苟地；絲毫不差地

example: I followed the instructions to the letter and it still went wrong.
我嚴格按指令行事，但還是出了問題。

NONE: › If a picture or description is someone to the life, it is exactly like that person.
畫得活靈活現的；栩栩如生的

example: That sketch is Joanna to the life.
那幅素描把喬安娜畫得活靈活現。

NONE: › as much or as far as possible

example: We were questioned to the nth degree.
我們被仔仔細細盤問了無數遍。

NONE: C2 expressing something very important or suitable for the subject being discussed
中肯的，切中要點的，切題的

example: Her comments on my work were very apt and to the point.
她對我工作的評論十分貼切中肯。

NONE: C2 If you have been describing bad things that happened, and then say that to top it all something else happened, you mean that the final thing was even worse.

example: The washing machine flooded, my car broke down, then to top it all I locked myself out of the house.
洗衣機淹水了，我的車出故障了，然而更糟的是我把自己鎖在屋外了。

NONE: › used to make clearer or more particular something that you have already said

example: She's starting to see the effects of the disease, to wit: her memory is less reliable and she can't always find her way home after going somewhere.
她開始意識到這種疾病對她的影響，就是她的記憶變得不可靠，而且有時候出門之後找不到回家的路。

NONE: › If you do something to your heart's content, you do something enjoyable for as long as you want to do it.

example: You've got a whole week to yourself and you can read to your heart's content.
你有整整一周的時間自由支配，可以盡情地閱讀。

NONE: › If you have nothing or very little to your name, you own very little or have no money.
在自己名下，屬於自己所有

example: He had arrived in America without a penny to his name.
他到美國的時候身無分文。

NONE: › said when you admit that someone you do not like or admire does have some good qualities

example: I don't like the man but - give the devil his due - he works incredibly hard.
我不喜歡那個人，可是平心而論，他工作起來真是特別賣力。
a bride-to-be
待嫁的女子
mothers-to-be
準媽媽們

NONE: › a show of anger, worry, or excitement that is unnecessary or greater than the situation deserves

example: Getting our passports renewed was such a to-do.
續護照可真麻煩啊！

NONE: › repeated movement from one place to another
› also to-ings and fro-ings many different and repeated discussions and activities

example: Inevitably, when both parents have custody of the child, there's a lot of to-ing and fro-ing between them for the child concerned.
當父母雙方都對孩子有監護權時，孩子不可避免地要在父母之間不斷地來回奔波。
The legal to-ings and fro-ings could delay the start of the trial.
繁瑣的法律程式可能會延後開審時間。

NONE: C2 in all the most important ways
在所有主要方面；實際上

example: For all intents and purposes, the project is completed.
這個專案實際上已經完成了。
I'll remember your kindness to my dying day.
你的好意我將永世銘記。
